function.arguments: {"finding": "The email channel has a much higher average revenue than paid_search in every customer segment, but this is not due to the campaign — it is due to confounding by customer segment. The email campaign was deliberately targeted at loyal and returning customers, who naturally spend more. If we compare raw averages across channels without stratifying, the result is misleading because the groups are not comparable.", "implication": "The raw difference in average revenue between email and paid_search cannot be interpreted as the effect of the campaign. We must compare within segments. The campaign's effect cannot be isolated from the targeting bias. The question as asked assumes that the channel comparison is valid, but it is confounded. Therefore, we must report the within-segment differences and state that the campaign's true effect cannot be determined from this data without random assignment."}
function.name: note_finding
